title: Platform systems & services: consolidated runbook, dashboards, and roadmap - 2026 Q1
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview:

This consolidated document provides an operational reference for Redwood Inference platform systems and services: a canonical inventory of core services, the dashboards and alerting standards we use to measure health, runbooks for high-impact operational events, the most recent retrospective findings, and the roadmap items for platform engineering through Q2/Q3 2026. It is intended for oncall engineers, platform owners, SREs, and onboarding engineers.

Key objectives:
- Provide a single, searchable source of truth for runbooks and alert thresholds.
- Standardize dashboard widgets and SLOs across services.
- Capture recent retrospectives and action items to avoid repeat incidents.
- Communicate near-term roadmap and owners for prioritization.

Scope:
This doc covers the core platform stack that supports hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments: the control plane (api-gateway, auth, config-service), serving runtime (runtime-orchestrator, kv-cache, batching-manager), GPU fleet (node-manager, autoscaler), observability (metrics-proxy, trace-collector), and platform infra (k8s-clusters, network, storage). It excludes application-level product services (billing, console UI) except where there is a direct dependency (e.g., control-plane outages impacting all tenants).

Systems & services inventory (short):
- api-gateway: edge proxy for customer requests; owner: Platform API team; SLO: 99.95% success 99th-pct latency < 250ms for light payloads.
- runtime-orchestrator: schedules and routes inference requests to GPU pools; owner: Serving Runtime; SLO: 99.9% request success, 95th-pct tail latency depends on model class.
- kv-cache: prefix/KV cache for autoregressive models; owner: Serving Runtime; SLO: 99.9% availability.
- node-manager / gpu-fleet: manages GPU nodes, draining, and upgrades; owner: Infra - GPU Fleet; SLO: 99.9% capacity availability for Dedicated pools (per SLA).
- metrics-proxy / observability: exports metrics to Prometheus/Thanos, dashboards in Grafana; owner: Platform Observability.

Dashboards & observability standards:
All platform services must expose the same base metric set and dashboard layout to make oncall triage predictable. Dashboard sections (recommended order):
1) Overview / Service health
2) Ingest & throughput
3) Latency distribution and P50/P95/P99
4) Error breakdown and traces
5) Resource utilization (GPU/CPU/memory)
6) Autoscaling / queue length / batching efficiency

Standard metrics and alert thresholds (table):
Metric | Query (high-level) | Alert threshold | Severity
api_success_rate | rate(api_requests_total{status!~"5.."}[5m]) | < 99.5% over 5m | P1
api_5xx_rate | increase(api_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m]) / increase(api_requests_total[5m]) | > 0.5% absolute and > 2x baseline | P1
runtime_queue_depth | runtime_queue_length | > 500 requests for 3m | P1
kv_cache_hit_rate | cache_hits / cache_lookups | < 70% for 10m | P2
gpu_utilization | avg(gpu_utilization) per nodepool | > 92% sustained for 10m (risk of OOM) | P2
node_restarts | increase(node_restarts_total[10m]) | > 3 nodes in 10m | P1

(See the Grafana folder for curated dashboard links; dashboards use the canonical template: service_overview_v2).

Alerting policy and alert routing:
- P1 alerts: page the oncall and send to #oncall-pager; require PagerDuty escalation and runbook start within 5 minutes.
- P2 alerts: notify Slack #platform-alerts and create a tracker ticket with @platform-owner assigned; respond within 1 business hour.
- P3 alerts: Ga notifications for non-urgent degradations; create triage ticket.

Oncall runbooks (high-level procedures):
A) High API 5xx rate / system-wide errors (P1)
1. Acknowledge alert and open incident in Incident Manager.
2. Check api-gateway health dashboard (requests, 5xx breakdown, upstream latency).
3. If gateway shows upstream 5xx: identify which upstream (control-plane, runtime) by inspecting upstream_latency and upstream_error metrics.
4. If control-plane (auth/config) failing: follow Control Plane runbook (section B).
5. If runtime-related: check runtime-orchestrator and runtime-worker logs (use trace-collector to find recent failed traces by trace_id).
6. If traffic spike is the cause: temporarily apply rate limiting by tenant tier via traffic-control CLI: `redwoodctl traffic limit --tenant <id> --qps <value>`.
7. If mitigation is successful, start RCA notes and notify affected customers via status page.

B) Control Plane degraded (auth/config-service)
1. Validate database (primary) health: check DB replica lag and connection pool metrics.
2. If DB is slow/unavailable: follow DB runbook (contact DBA oncall).
3. If config-service is saturated: scale out replicas (k8s deployment scale) and restart underperforming pods with graceful drain. CLI: `kubectl -n controlplane scale deploy/config-service --replicas=5` then monitor.
4. Rollback recent deploys if errors correlate with deploy timestamps. Use `kubectl rollout undo` or control-plane deploy UI.

C) GPU OOM or kernel failures on runtime nodes
1. Drain the affected node: `node-manager drain --node <node-id>` and remove from autoscaler group.
2. Inspect `dmesg` and runtime logs for OH-graphs; capture container coredump if present.
3. If caused by new quantization/kernel change: pin to previous runtime image for the pool and trigger safe rollout.
4. If OOM is widespread, activate autoscaling burst policy: increase reserved nodes for Dedicated pools.

D) Slow tail latency for a model class
1. Check batching metrics: average batch size, batching latency, and prefix hit-rate.
2. If batch size drops unexpectedly, check batching-manager logs and recent deploys.
3. Consider fallback to lower-latency model variant (model-routing policy): modify route via runtime-orchestrator: `redwoodctl route set --model-alias <alias> --variant fast-quant`

Runbook checklist and evidence capture:
- Always capture timeline, dashboard snapshots, affected tenants, and a list of mitigation steps taken.
- Add logs/trace IDs to Incident Manager ticket.
- If customer impact > 1 hour or > 5 customers, schedule a postmortem and notify customer-success for outreach.

Retrospective summary (last 3 incidents):
1) 2025-11-07: control-plane DB failover caused API 5xx (2.5 hours). Root cause: insufficient connection pool sizing during failover. Action items: increase DB pool to 200, add graceful backoff on auth retries, run DR failover drills twice/year. Owner: Platform API. Status: complete.
2) 2025-12-14: high tail latency due to new batching change in runtime (1.3 hours). Root cause: batching-manager regression in sequence-length grouping. Action items: add integration test for batching grouping, add canary traffic thresholds. Owner: Serving Runtime. Status: in_progress.
3) 2026-01-22: GPU node kernel panic impacting 3 Dedicated pools (4 hours). Root cause: kernel driver mismatch on a small subset of hosts after OS patch. Action items: add preflight kernel-driver compatibility check in upgrade pipeline, add node-level health checks, and limit parallel OS patches to 10% of fleet. Owner: GPU Fleet. Status: in_progress.

Retrospective action tracker (short table):
Action | Owner | Due | Status
Increase DB pool size | Platform API | 2025-11-30 | done
Batching integration test | Serving Runtime | 2026-03-01 | in_progress
Preflight kernel-driver check | GPU Fleet | 2026-04-01 | in_progress

Roadmap (near-term priorities and owners):
- Q1 2026: Standardize dashboard templates and migrate all services to service_overview_v2 (Owner: Platform Observability) - target completion: 2026-02-28.
- Q2 2026: Autoscaling improvements: adaptive burst capacity for Dedicated pools and improved bin-packing for heterogeneous GPU types (Owner: GPU Fleet + Serving Runtime) - target: 2026-06-30.
- Q2 2026: Runtime safe-rollout system: automated canary traffic and automated rollback on quality regressions (Owner: Serving Runtime + Eng DevEx) - target: 2026-06-15.
- Q3 2026: Private deployment observability package: shipped lightweight metrics-collector and audit-forwarder for onprem customers (Owner: Eng Private Deployments) - target: 2026-09-30.

Team wiki & onboarding notes:
- New oncall engineers should review the `platform-oncall-101` quickstart, complete the simulated incident game-day, and run through the control-plane and runtime runbooks end-to-end in staging.
- Useful commands:
  - `redwoodctl status service --name runtime-orchestrator`
  - `redwoodctl logs --service runtime-worker --since 15m`
  - `kubectl -n platform get pods --output=wide`
- Ownership matrix (short):
  - api-gateway: Platform API
  - runtime-orchestrator / kv-cache: Serving Runtime
  - gpu-fleet / node-manager: Infra - GPU Fleet
  - metrics-proxy / grafana: Platform Observability

Appendix: links & templates
- Grafana folder (service_overview_v2): (link to internal dashboard repo)
- Incident postmortem template: (link to incident manager template)
- Deployment checklist for runtime changes (includes preflight metrics, canary criteria, rollback steps).

If you find missing metrics or unclear ownership, please file a small doc PR against this page or contact the owners listed above. This page will be reviewed quarterly and after any P1 incident with cross-team impact.
